test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In Natya Shastra, Bharat Muni has clubbed musical instruments into how many groups?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Instruments** were categorised into **four groups in Bharat Muni's Natya Shastra **(written between 200 BC and 200 AD): **Avanaddha Vadya** (membranophones or percussion instruments), **Ghan Vadya **(idiophones or solid instruments), **Sushir Vadya **(aerophones or wind instruments), and **Tat Vadya **(solid instruments) (chordophones or stringed instruments).
 
• This historic classification of Indian musical instruments devised by Bharat Muni was later applied to the musical instruments of Europe in the 12th century.
 
• The four divisions were later given Greek names: Chordophones for Tat Vadya, Membranophones for Avanaddha Vadya, Aerophones for Sushir Vadya, and Autophones for Ghan Vadya.
 
• As a result, the Natya Shastra is the foundation for the western classification system. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The musical treatise Natya Shastra is typically credited to **the ancient sage Bharata Muni.**
 
• The book discusses Sanskrit theatre as well as ancient Indian dramaturgy and histrionics. Bharata is regarded as the originator of Indian theatre.
 
• Although estimates range from 500 BCE to 500 CE, he is dated to between 200 BCE and 200 CE.
